entries.name: Your Eyes In Space — advertised mit-final tag
entries.license: MIT for mit-final and earlier; current main AGPL-3.0-or-later
entries.notes: Current LICENSE says mit-final and earlier are MIT, but the remote tag is not currently exposed/resolvable. Do not select by tag name; use the separately verified e520568 MIT commit entry.

entries.name: Cosmos browser universe engine
entries.notes: Current MIT main audited locally on 2026-11-22. Strong modular engine: camera-relative coordinates, scale regimes, tile streaming, shaders, tests, thin React canvas. Internal packages compile and Vite bundle runs, but repo-wide typecheck currently fails in SearchPanel on stale ApiEntity fields; full star-tile data also expects a backend manifest. Better subsystem donor than immediate mother product today.

entries.name: Solar Wanderer
entries.notes: Candidate for scale/travel subsystem if a full-solution backbone is not selected.

entries.name: SpaceKit.js
entries.notes: Prefer extracting orbital math/data pieces over adopting its renderer lifecycle wholesale.

entries.name: Galaxy Explorer
entries.notes: Already reused in the current V2 galaxy renderer.

entries.name: Helios procedural star-system generator
entries.notes: Already reused in the current V2 deterministic generator decomposition.

entries.name: ProceduralPlanets
entries.notes: Already integrated; baked mode is the default for scalable ordinary worlds.

entries.name: ProceduralTerrains
entries.notes: Preserved as an optional Hero-surface experiment, not a universal surface requirement.

entries.name: @pmndrs/sky
entries.notes: Potential future WebGPU branch; current main stack is not yet a clean compatibility fit.

entries.name: three-nebula
entries.notes: Candidate effect system; only adopt if the chosen backbone does not already cover these effects.

entries.name: Your Eyes In Space — verified MIT commit e520568
entries.license: MIT source at e520568; bundled HYG-derived stars.bin is CC BY-SA 4.0; NASA assets/data retain their own notices
covers: deterministic procedural star field and systems
entries.notes: Code-level and runtime verified on 2026-11-22: npm ci/build passes; headless browser boots; a minimal public registerExtraSystem patch successfully injected HELION + AURORA-01 and the stock renderer displayed the Hero planet. Main bundle ~2.54 MB; 449 MB dist is dominated by optional lessons/tours (~389 MB) that are not needed for Personal Universe. Additional renderer PoC on 2026-11-22: StarPoints + ProcStarPoints + GalaxyCloud + GalaxySprites + CameraController + Input ran inside the same React Three Fiber 8 / Three 0.185.1 Canvas with logarithmicDepthBuffer; strict TS, Vite build and headless runtime all passed, rendering the 109,401-star catalog without a second canvas.

entries.name: NASA Exoplanet Archive TAP / pscomppars
entries.license: NASA public scientific data / archive terms; attribution retained
entries.notes: Already used by Personal Universe. TAP schema exposes hip_name, hd_name and gaia_dr3_id in pscomppars; 2026-11-22 research found 51/64 nearest snapshot hosts have HIP identifiers and all 51 exactly match the vendored HYG-derived YEIS star binary.

entries.name: React Three Fiber
entries.notes: Current project host. Research PoC proved YEIS renderer classes can attach directly to R3F's existing scene/gl/camera instead of running a second WebGL application.

entries.name: Astro Content Collections / Content Layer
entries.notes: Already available through the installed Astro runtime. Astro 7 provides built-in glob() and file() loaders plus Zod 4 schemas; no new runtime dependency is required for local portfolio content.

entries.name: Keystatic
entries.notes: Good optional authoring UI because it can manage files that Astro Content Collections already consume. Current project does not yet need an embedded editor, so avoid its extra packages/Markdoc/config until authoring friction appears.

entries.name: TinaCMS
entries.notes: Strong visual-editing workflow but existing-site integration adds Tina packages and commonly SSR adapter/island plumbing. Too broad for a static single-owner portfolio content layer at this stage.

entries.name: Decap CMS
entries.notes: Mature Git-based admin UI, but requires an admin surface and backend/auth configuration while still leaving frontend content modeling/placement to the site. Keep as an editor option, not the current foundation.

entries.name: cmdk + Fuse.js navigation/search stack
entries.notes: Candidate supplement only. It would duplicate YEIS astronomical indexes if used as the primary universe navigator.

entries.name: Pagefind
entries.notes: Useful later for article/document search, but not a replacement for YEIS spatial destination search.

entries.name: GitHub Actions PR-diff gate with required status checks
entries.notes: Use the repository-local Node policy engine inside GitHub Actions, but evaluate the PR commit range instead of only a dirty working tree. Pair with a required status check so changing or deleting the workflow cannot silently bypass merge gating.

entries.name: Rendezvous / Highest Random Weight (HRW) hashing
entries.license: Algorithm/reference; RFC text under IETF terms
covers: minimal remapping when destinations are added or removed
entries.notes: Selected as the placement primitive for Personal Signals. Unlike modulo-N, HRW ranks each stable destination identity per content key, so adding/removing a star changes only mappings that genuinely prefer the changed destination.

entries.name: hrw-hash JavaScript package
entries.notes: Very small and dependency-free, but Personal Universe only needs one narrow deterministic score primitive. Prefer the standard HRW algorithm directly to avoid another runtime dependency unless future weighted/ranked APIs justify the package.

entries.name: Jump Consistent Hash
covers: minimal remapping as bucket count changes
entries.notes: Excellent for sequentially numbered buckets, but less appropriate for Personal Universe because star destinations are identity-addressed and can be inserted/removed independently rather than only appended as dense bucket numbers.
